title: ET Startup Awards 2026 Names Nominees for Comeback Kid and Best on Campus
excerpt: India's 12th annual startup awards shortlist ten ventures spanning solar energy, logistics, AI, spacetech, and robotics across two marquee categories.
body:
• Five startups — SolarSquare, Shadowfax, Scapia, Emergent, and Pratilipi — are nominated for the Comeback Kid award, which celebrates entrepreneurs who rebuilt or launched more successful businesses after setbacks.
  • Five student-founded ventures — Qosmic, Armatrix, Panoculon Labs, Dream Aerospace, and Plenome Technologies — compete for Best on Campus.
  • Nominees span solar energy, logistics, travel fintech, AI app building, spacetech, robotics, and privacy-first AI infrastructure.
  • Bengaluru dominates the shortlist with seven of ten nominees headquartered in the city.

The Economic Times has announced nominees for two of the eight categories in the 12th annual ET Startup Awards: Comeback Kid, which honors entrepreneurs who survived failure and rebuilt, and Best on Campus, which spotlights student-founded companies with commercial validation through investors or paying customers.

Comeback Kid: Five Stories of Reinvention

The Comeback Kid shortlist features five companies whose founders navigated significant business pivots or early adversity to find traction.

SolarSquare, a Mumbai-based residential rooftop solar company founded in 2015 by Shreya Mishra, Neeraj Jain, and Nikhil Nahar, now operates across 20 Indian cities. Backed by B Capital, Lightspeed, and Elevation Capital, the company sells, installs, and monitors home solar systems while helping customers access financing and government subsidies.

Shadowfax, also founded in 2015, is now publicly listed — a milestone for a logistics company that started as a hyperlocal delivery outfit in Bengaluru. Co-founded by Abhishek Bansal, Vaibhav Khandelwal, Praharsh Chandra, and Gaurav Jaithlia, it provides express parcel, reverse logistics, and hyperlocal delivery to e-commerce marketplaces and direct-to-consumer brands.

"Backed by B Capital, Lightspeed, and Elevation Capital, the company sells, installs, and monitors home solar systems while helping customers access financing and government subsidies."

Scapia, a Bengaluru-based travel fintech platform founded in 2022 by former Flipkart executive Anil Goteti, combines credit card spending, travel bookings, rewards, UPI transactions, and airport privileges in a single app. Its backers include General Catalyst, Peak XV Partners, Z47, and Elevation Capital.

Emergent, co-headquartered in Bengaluru and San Francisco, is an AI app-building platform founded in 2024 by Mukund Jha. It lets non-technical users create web and mobile applications through prompts, with the platform handling coding, hosting, deployment, and debugging. Its investor roster includes Creaegis, Khosla Ventures, SoftBank, Lightspeed, and Together Fund.

Pratilipi, founded in 2015 by Ranjeet Pratap Singh, Sankaranarayanan Devarajan, and Sahradayi Modi, is an Indian-language storytelling platform that monetizes by licensing stories for television, streaming, films, and short-form video while sharing revenue with writers. It is backed by Jungle Ventures, Krafton, Omidyar Network, and Nexus Venture Partners.

Best on Campus: Student Founders Building Deep Tech

The Best on Campus category showcases student founders whose ventures have gained validation from investors or paying customers.

Qosmic, a Bengaluru-based spacetech startup founded in 2025 by Shreyaans Jain, Rohit Ramakrishnan, and Aloke Kumar, is tackling data bottlenecks between space and Earth. Its technology aims to enable satellites to transmit data faster and in much larger volumes. The company is backed by Prosus, Accel, and South Park Commons.

Armatrix, also based in Bengaluru and founded in 2024, builds snake-like robotic arms designed to enter cramped and hazardous industrial spaces. Co-founded by Vishrant Dave, Ayush Ranjan, and Prateesh Awasthi, the company has applications planned across aviation, oil and gas, and nuclear industries.

Panoculon Labs, a 2023 Bengaluru startup co-founded by Rishabh Sharma and Sreeraj R, builds vision hardware for robots and AI systems. Its Trinet device captures first-person visual data for training autonomous robots. The company is also developing AI-powered smart glasses for visually impaired users.

Dream Aerospace, the lone non-Bengaluru entry among the campus picks, was founded in 2022 in Kanpur by Hari Krishnan KJ and Rogith Srinivasan. The company develops green-propellant satellite propulsion systems aimed at the growing low-Earth orbit market.

Plenome Technologies, based in Chennai and founded in 2023 by Prabhu Rajagopal, Anirudh Varna, and Vijayaraja R, builds AI infrastructure that lets companies train and deploy models on sensitive data without moving it outside their own systems. Its Ashwin AI product is a multilingual voice copilot for clinical documentation.

Bengaluru's Dominance and the Diaspora Connection

Seven of the ten nominees are headquartered in Bengaluru, underscoring the city's continued grip on India's startup ecosystem. Emergent's dual presence in Bengaluru and San Francisco highlights the cross-border talent and capital flows that connect Indian startup founders with Silicon Valley investors — a pipeline closely watched by NRI investors and diaspora professionals tracking India's tech evolution.

The ET Startup Awards recognize excellence across eight categories, including Startup of the Year, Woman Ahead, Top Innovator, Bootstrap Champ, Midas Touch, and Social Enterprise. Winners will be announced at the main event.
